audits.title: 315 Chaperone Documentation in The Breast Clinic: A Closed Loop Audit
audits.standard: GMC and Chelsea & Westminster Trust guidelines: consent, chaperone use/refusal, and chaperone role and identity documented
audits.setting: Breast clinic, West Middlesex University Hospital

cycle1.result: Consent 0%; chaperone identity 12%; chaperone role 8%; chaperone use/refusal 27%.

audits.intervention: Teaching to breast MDT, introduction of electronic notes (Cerner) and an instructional video on creating an automatic documentation template.

cycle2.result: Consent 38% (p < 0.0001); identity 35% (p = 0.0003); role 23% (p = 0.0091); use/refusal 35% (p = 0.3305, not significant).

audits.other_findings: Documentation remained suboptimal; recommended a mandatory e-notes template and more chaperone staff.
audits.citation: Maden C, Lee A, Kelly M, Im Y, Barkeji M. 315 Chaperone Documentation in The Breast Clinic: A Closed Loop Audit. British Journal of Surgery. 2021;108(Supplement_6). doi:10.1093/bjs/znab259.037.

audits.title: EP.TH.507An Audit of Consent Documentation and Chaperone Use in Patients Presenting to Acute Settings with Breast Complaints
audits.standard: GMC, Royal College of Emergency Medicine and Royal College of Surgeons standards on consent and chaperones
audits.setting: Emergency department and surgical assessment unit (Glasgow Royal Infirmary)

cycle1.result: Consent documented in 7 (11%); chaperone offered in 17 (27%), with name and role of chaperone documented on 11 occasions.

audits.other_findings: Male examiners offered a chaperone 50% of the time versus 6% for female examiners.
audits.citation: Dunlop H. EP.TH.507An Audit of Consent Documentation and Chaperone Use in Patients Presenting to Acute Settings with Breast Complaints. British Journal of Surgery. 2021;108(Supplement_7). doi:10.1093/bjs/znab309.057.

audits.title: 871 Audit on Compliance and Documentation of GMC Guidelines Regarding the Use of Chaperone During the Intimate Examination
audits.standard: GMC guidance on chaperones during intimate examination
audits.setting: General surgery, surgical assessment unit and ED, Royal Sussex County Hospital

cycle1.result: 9/168 (5.3%) had chaperone documentation, of which 1/9 (11%) complete; perianal examination 1/23 (4.3%); abdominal examination 8/141 (5.6%).

audits.intervention: Results shared with the department with education; chaperone stickers (name, position, gender) to be attached to notes.
audits.other_findings: All 9 documented cases were male doctors examining female patients; prospective post-intervention data collection ongoing.
audits.citation: Singh A, Siby J, Subramanian A, Janakan G. 871 Audit on Compliance and Documentation of GMC Guidelines Regarding the Use of Chaperone During the Intimate Examination. British Journal of Surgery. 2023;110(Supplement_7). doi:10.1093/bjs/znad258.388.

audits.title: An audit of chaperone use for intimate examinations in an integrated sexual health clinic.
audits.standard: GMC guidance on chaperones for intimate examinations
audits.setting: Non-specialist morning clinics, Chalmers Sexual Health Centre, Edinburgh

cycle1.result: 20 of 104 genital examinations recorded as chaperoned; chaperone declined documented in 5; 24% had documentation of chaperone presence or offer.

audits.title: Documentation of chaperone presence in breast clinic, a complete audit cycle.
audits.standard: GMC and Irish Medical Council: chaperone for intimate examinations, clearly documented

cycle1.result: Chaperone present 100% when male doctor examined female patient, but documented in 0/126 charts

audits.intervention: Chaperone stamp in medical notes, educational email with GMC/IMC guidance and posters in clinic rooms
audits.other_findings: At 1 week documentation was 80% (51/64). Survey: 50% of doctors did not know documentation was necessary and 25% forgot.
audits.citation: Alameer A, Mohammed A, Elwahab SA, Boland M, Elfadul A, Tiwary T, et al.. Documentation of chaperone presence in breast clinic, a complete audit cycle. Ir J Med Sci. 2022;191(2):637-639. doi:10.1007/s11845-021-02634-y. PMID: 33970393.

audits.title: Sustainable quality improvement interventions to ensure adequate documentation of chaperone presence in breast clinic: A multi-cycle clinical audit.
audits.standard: Best practice guidelines on chaperone presence and its documentation during intimate examination
audits.setting: Tertiary breast referral clinic, Beaumont Hospital, Dublin

cycle1.result: Chaperone presence was observed in 100% of consultations but documented in only 7.6%.

audits.intervention: First a 'chaperone stamp' in the notes before consultation; then, after moving to electronic records, a mandatory check field for chaperone documentation.

cycle2.result: Mandatory electronic check field achieved 100% documentation of chaperone presence.

audits.other_findings: Three cycles, 388 patients in total; the stamp improved documentation by 51.1% but this fell by 13.6% at six months.
audits.citation: Hehir CM, Calpin GG, Walsh N, Daly GR, Dowling GP, Hembrecht S, et al.. Sustainable quality improvement interventions to ensure adequate documentation of chaperone presence in breast clinic: A multi-cycle clinical audit. Int J Qual Health Care. 2026. doi:10.1093/intqhc/mzag141. PMID: 42765530.

audits.title: An audit on the use of chaperones during intimate patient examinations.
audits.standard: GMC: all intimate examinations should be chaperoned and chaperone identity documented in the notes
audits.setting: Surgical assessment unit (Royal Stoke University Hospital)

cycle1.result: Chaperone documentation in 13 notes (21.3%); chaperone use documented in 10 (16.4%), identity in 9 (14.8%), decline in 3 (4.9%).

audits.intervention: Chaperone sticker and posters as an aide-memoire.

cycle2.result: Chaperone documentation in 32 notes (60.3%, p = 0.0001); use 27 (50.9%), identity 20 (37.7%), decline 5 (9.4%).

audits.other_findings: Further audit planned after surgical proformas are redesigned with a chaperone signature area.
audits.citation: Sharma N, Kathleen Mary Walsh A, Rajagopalan S. An audit on the use of chaperones during intimate patient examinations. Ann Med Surg (Lond). 2016;7:58-60. doi:10.1016/j.amsu.2016.03.005. PMID: 27076910.
